item.content:encoded:
Two medium-large nits to pick.

First, containment is both too much and not enough. Too much because constant, multi-redundant monitoring isn't necessary. Lock it in a standard safe and be done1. Not enough because this would require zero visibility protocols for transportation, experimentation, and recovery after breach. The sort of steps taken in the experiment log should be included in the containment write up.

Second, the subject is presumed to have died of thirst? Go and check his pulse for crying out loud; and then do an autopsy to confirm cause of death. Leaving a loose thread that huge is just bad science.

Footnotes
1. This also makes it Safe, in my opinion.

Water is also a worldly possession, which D-501 just renounced ownership of with the exception of SCP-501.
It could very well be a typo, however, its also quite possible that he died not because his body failed due to lack of hydration but because he violated the oath by desiring water.

item.content:encoded:
Why guard/film/stare at a black box all the time if the object within only affects anyone that sees it? Nothing is mentioned that necessitates additional containment procedures beyond locking it in a box and making sure no one opens said box. Which would also make this Safe, not Euclid. Moreover, a containment breach in its glorious entirety would be one person, sitting in front of a (formerly) locked box, staring at the object naked and hairless. Until he or she dies of thirst. Or sepsis. So not only is it containable, it is easily recontainable.

I like the rest of the article, beyond the containment procedures, because it's a simple and neat concept that is well executed. Null vote, until it's either edited or someone convinces me that I'm being unreasonable.
